paras: The mock hanging of five men at Las Vegas, New Mexico, took place about midnight on Saturday, 4 February 1882, when a group of East Side citizens seized Cal. Jones, Tobe Johnson, Ed. Patters and two men known as Roxy and Buck and pulled each of them up by a noose. The men were released alive and left town, and the Las Vegas Daily Gazette praised the act as a lesson to "thugs and dead-beats."

According to the Gazette, there had been "an evident accumulation of thugs and dead-beats in the city" for some time. The paper called the recent robbery of a discharged soldier "the culmination of this lawlessness" and a "good excuse" for the East Side's citizens to act. The article did not say that any of the five men had taken part in the robbery, and it gave no race for them.

About twelve o'clock on Saturday night, "a goodly number of citizens" took the five men to a point a little north of the round house. There the men were taken one at a time and pulled up by a noose until their feet swung clear of the ground, and this was repeated several times with each of them. The hangings were meant, the Gazette said, as a warning to men with "no visible means of gaining a livelihood," and once the noose was removed they "lit out at a lively rate."
No report of arrests or an official response appears in the coverage.

The Las Vegas Daily Gazette ran the story on 7 February 1882 under the heading "They Skipped," directly after an item on a separate fatal shooting. The paper called the five men "whelps" and joked about giving them a taste of how it goes "to stand on nothing and kick at the United States." It closed by calling the treatment "a good lesson for such fellows" and said the remedy "can not be applied too often."
No other paper was found to have carried the story, and no follow-up report appears in the coverage.

bases: A group of citizens seized five men, pulled each up by a noose until his feet cleared the ground, released them and warned them out of town; no one was killed (A1).

The 'goodly number of citizens' acted without lawful authority and on the pretext of ridding the town of 'thugs and dead-beats', but the five men were let go alive after a mock hanging, so no one was killed (A1).
Only the local Las Vegas Daily Gazette item reports the episode; no other paper or follow-up was found (A1).
